text: A set is an unordered collection of unique values, with real maths built in.
Duplicates simply cannot exist in a set — adding one again changes nothing.
We define two sets that share the numbers three and four.
Ampersand is intersection — only the elements found in both.
That gives us three and four, the overlap.
Pipe is union, every element from either side, with duplicates collapsed.
Union is how you merge two collections and forget about overlap entirely.
Minus is difference, what's in a but not in b.
Passing a list to set is the fastest way to remove duplicates.
Six items become three, though the order is not guaranteed.
And membership tests are near instant, because sets are hash based, not scanned.
Checking membership in a list scans it; in a set it's a single hash lookup.
